name: Druze faith
title: The story of the Druze faith

text: The Druze faith began more than 1,000 years ago in Cairo, in Egypt.
There a scholar named Hamza ibn Ali began to preach that God is one.
src: The Druze faith arose in Cairo in 1017
Hamza ibn Ali began in 1017 to preach a Muwaḥḥidūn (Unitarian) doctrine / God is one in strict and uncompromising unity

text: The Druze call themselves al-Muwaḥḥidūn, which means “the monotheists”, people who believe in one God.
Their faith grew out of Islam, but most Druze do not see themselves as Muslims.
src: The Druze, who call themselves al-Muwaḥḥidūn, “the monotheists”, hold to the strict unity of God
their faith grew out of Ismāʿīlī Islam, but most Druze do not identify as Muslims

text: The Druze believe that when a person dies, their soul passes at once into a new body.
Only the ʻuqqāl, “the wise”, fewer than one in ten Druze, may read the holy books.
src: At death the soul passes at once into a new human body
only the initiated ʻuqqāl read its holy books / the ʻuqqāl, “the wise”, men and women together making up less than 10% of the community

text: Soon after it began, the Fatimid rulers attacked the Druze, and the faith went into hiding.
Later, Druze lords from the Chouf, in Mount Lebanon, helped shape the history of the region.
src: the regent Sitt al-Mulk ordered the army to destroy the movement in 1021 / facing repeated persecution from Fatimid, Mamluk and Ottoman rulers / The faith went underground
From the Chouf of Mount Lebanon and later the Jabal al-Druze, Druze lords and fighters helped shape the history of the Levant

text: About 100 years ago, Sultan Pasha al-Atrash led the Druze in a revolt against French rule in Syria.
Today there are between 800,000 and one million Druze, living mainly in Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Jordan.
src: Under Sultan Pasha al-Atrash the Druze provide much of the military force of the Syrian Revolution against French rule / In Syria Sultan Pasha al-Atrash led the Druze in the Syrian Revolution of 1925–27
